layers.message: Record directory search scope and design
Add email search with shared normalization

problemsMatch: assigned checkpoint requires Assessment Purpose INCREMENT and target Increment 2

graderOnly: DEV-001's code in src/search.js was rewritten while adding DEV-002 (commit Add email search with shared normalization): name matching now goes through src/normalize.js and every name match carries matchedOn name, so the Increment 1 evidence recorded against the earlier src/search.js blob is stale.

The architecture (Interfaces and Contracts, Technical Acceptance Criteria for AC-001 and AC-002, Build Plan step 2) requires every result, including name matches, to have exactly id, name, email, and matchedOn, so the AC-001 test 'finds people by any part of their name, ignoring case' in test/search.test.js, which deep-equals the old three-key shape, is obsolete rather than catching a regression.
That obsolete test is the only failing test: node --test test/search.test.js reports 1 pass and 1 fail, and test/directory.test.js passes.
src/search.js and src/normalize.js at the last commit implement the design correctly for AC-001 and AC-002; there is no implementation defect for the grouped Increment 2 outcome.

The prior report allocates 2 of 8 scenarios to src/search.js (the obsolete name-match scenario and the no-match scenario): the user approved a targeted increase to 8 for src/search.js only. src/normalize.js is a new source file with no allocations yet and the default limit of five.

selfChecks.cmd: node --input-type=module -e 'const assert = (await import(`node:assert/strict`)).default; const { searchUsers } = await import(`./src/search.js`); const u = [{ id: 1, name: `Grace Hopper`, email: `grace.hopper@example.org` }, { id: 2, name: `Ada Lovelace`, email: `ada@example.org` }, { id: 5, name: `Bob Stone`, email: `ada.stone@example.org` }]; assert.deepEqual(searchUsers(u, `AD`), [{ id: 2, name: `Ada Lovelace`, email: `ada@example.org`, matchedOn: `name` }, { id: 5, name: `Bob Stone`, email: `ada.stone@example.org`, matchedOn: `email` }]); assert.deepEqual(searchUsers(u, ` HOPPER@ `).map((r) => r.id + r.matchedOn), [`1email`]); assert.deepEqual(searchUsers(u, `ada  love`).map((r) => r.id), [2]); assert.deepEqual(searchUsers(u, `   `), []);'
selfChecks.why: the current implementation satisfies the design contract for name and email search (shape, ordering, normalization, blank query)

notes: Standalone brownfield fixture. 00-project: staff-directory Node library (src/directory.js, data/users.json, test/directory.test.js). 50-scope-design: Auditor context, scope (AC-001 name search, AC-002 email search with matched field, AC-003 paging), design whose Interfaces, Technical Acceptance Criteria, and Build Plan step 2 require matchedOn on every result and shared normalization; STATE at DEVELOPING with a pending INCREMENTAL cadence request. 60-increment-1: approved INCREMENTAL plan (Increments 1: DEV-001/AC-001; 2: DEV-001, DEV-002/AC-001, AC-002; 3: DEV-003/AC-003), src/search.js v1 returning {id,name,email}; CHECKPOINT Increment 1. 70-verify-increment-1: test/search.test.js (2 scenarios charged to src/search.js), package.json test script, verification report IN_PROGRESS / INCREMENT / Increment 1 with Increment 1 VERIFIED, prior blob/commit identities, AC-002 and AC-003 AWAITING_IMPLEMENTATION; CHECKPOINT back to DEVELOPING. 80-increment-2: src/search.js rewritten (DEV-001 reopened and DONE again), new src/normalize.js, plan Current Increment 2 with DEV-001/DEV-002 DONE and self-checks, DEV-003 PENDING; STATE TESTING, CHECKPOINT from DEVELOPING, Reason Increment 2 ready. The full check fails only because the report still targets Increment 1 (deliberate, per catalog); the turn-end check accepts it.
